title: Unified invocation contract mart with incremental backfill and schema evolution plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: build a single, query-optimized 'invocation_contract' mart that consolidates per-route invocation records, tenant attribution, model-variant metadata and runtime cost signals. This mart will be the authoritative source for Console dashboards, cost/latency attribution jobs, and downstream experiments. Deliverables: (1) canonical table schema with explicit contract fields, partitioning and compaction strategy, (2) incremental materialized view (mview) recipe for daily/real-time pipelines, (3) safe backfill plan for historical data with rate-limited jobs, (4) schema evolution policy and contract for downstream consumers. Motivation: current queries scatter across multiple denormalized tables, causing inconsistent SLA/cost numbers, expensive ad-hoc joins and brittle dashboards. A curated mart reduces query complexity, improves latency for dashboards and enables deterministic cost attribution per route/tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical invocation_contract table defined in Iceberg/BigQuery with documented column descriptions and data types
Daily incremental mview that refreshes within SLO (<30m) for last 48h and supports point-in-time backfills
Backfill tool able to process historical 18 months of raw events at <= 20% cluster impact (throttled jobs)
Migration guide and compatibility shim for Console dashboards and alerts, with a rollback path
End-to-end tests and lineage registered in the data catalog; alerting for schema drift and mview freshness
implementation_notes: Design choices: use Iceberg-managed tables with hourly partitioning on event_date + tenant_id bucketing for even distribution. Store canonical enums for route_type/model_variant to avoid repeated string decoding. Keep raw_invocation_id and invocation_trace pointers for debugging. We will maintain a lightweight change-log table (invocation_contract_delta) for fast incremental refreshes. For cost attribution, precompute per-token cost fields during ingestion using the latest pricing function, with ability to recompute for audit. Use compacted hourly files to optimize small-query latency. See design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/789012345/Unified+Invocation+Contract+Mart
tradeoffs: Denormalization vs storage: reducing join complexity increases storage by ~15% but lowers CPU on dashboards
Immediate replay vs eventual reprice: storing precomputed cost simplifies queries but requires recomputation jobs when pricing changes
Iceberg vs BigQuery managed: Iceberg gives stronger schema evolution controls (preferred) but requires additional operator automation
migration_plan: Phase 1: Create invocation_contract_v1 and start populating via streaming pipeline in parallel with current tables (no consumer cutover). Phase 2: Backfill historical data month-by-month using throttled Spark jobs; validate rowcounts and key-aggregates against existing aggregates. Phase 3: Point specific dashboards to _v1 (canary subset of orgs), run a 2-week parity window. Phase 4: Swap aliases and deprecate old tables after 30 days. Rollback: switch alias back and re-enable old dashboards. Backfill runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleBackfillRunbook
monitoring_and_slos: Freshness SLOs: last-12h data <10m lag, last-48h data <30m lag. Validation metrics: daily row-count delta, per-tenant route coverage, cost-sum parity. Alerts: freshness breach, partition skew, schema drift. Dashboard: curated 'Invocations Health' in Console (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345)
data_quality_checks: Per-tenant event-rate sanity checks (3-sigma anomaly detection)
Hourly reconciliation: sum(token_count) vs raw_event_token_agg within 0.5%
Foreign-key existence checks for tenant_id and model_variant ids
